answer: In an AI-agent marketplace at a river port, a quill seller accepts orders only through a registry that locks refundable deposits and allocates order capacity in proportion to deposited funds, not identity count. The deposit is a scarce-resource signal: splitting $1,000 among a thousand fake agents yields no more capacity than one agent staking $1,000. To gain capacity, an attacker must lock additional capital and forgo its use elsewhere.
